verdicts.claim: By default SQLite runs a checkpoint automatically when the WAL reaches 1000 pages; all automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE, and PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0 disables them
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages'; 'automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE'; pragma.html: 'zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off'

verdicts.claim: Overlapping readers that leave no gap mean no checkpoint can complete and the WAL file grows without bound (checkpoint starvation)
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound'

verdicts.claim: FULL ... checkpoints everything and syncs, blocking new writers but not new readers
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.'

verdicts.claim: Only TRUNCATE mode or PRAGMA journal_size_limit (default -1, applied per database on each WAL reset) reduces the on-disk size
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit)'; 'the write-ahead log file is not truncated following a checkpoint'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(mode) returns one row of three integers: busy flag (1 if a FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked)... -1 when no WAL
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'single row with three integer columns'; 'will be 1 if a RESTART or FULL or TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked'; 'second and third column are -1 if there is no write-ahead log'

verdicts.claim: With synchronous=NORMAL in WAL mode... A checkpoint of FULL or higher (or one synchronous=FULL transaction) makes earlier commits durable
verdicts.evidence: forum: 'FULL or above is sufficient to ensure durability of previously-committed transactions'; Hipp: synchronous=FULL txn 'makes all prior transactions durable'; wal.html: checkpoint 'the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync'

verdicts.claim: if another connection is already checkpointing, the call returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately and the busy handler is not invoked; busy-handler give-up degrades to PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case'; busy-handler returns 0 -> continues 'in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE'

verdicts.claim: WAL-reset bug affects 3.7.0 through 3.51.2, and is fixed in 3.51.3 with backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2'; 'fixed in version 3.51.3'; 'Backports ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7' (source hedges with 'likely')

verdicts.claim: Antithesis reproduced it in about 15 minutes on 3.51.2 ... same workload ran clean on 3.51.3. Tailscale ... spent roughly six months of 2025 on outages
verdicts.evidence: antithesis: 'Antithesis caught the bug in 15 mins'; '3.51.3 comes back clean'; 'Tailscale suffered 6 months of shaky uptime' re 2025; 'developers have never been able to reproduce the bug organically'

verdicts.claim: Syncthing found its timer-based checkpointer might never see a window without an active reader ... positive feedback loop and grind to a halt
verdicts.evidence: syncthing (2026-02-06): 'we might never hit a timewindow without an active reader'; 'positive feedback loop and database operations grind to a halt'; 'truncate the WAL would mandate some kind of exclusive locking'
